Subject: MSA & Order Form — private hosting operator access and audit exhibits

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and Legal at BridgeMed have one consolidated ask before we can sign: we need explicit contract language and an exhibit for private hosting that covers operator access, snapshot transfer/verification, and an escrow-like custody pathway for a forensic snapshot if certain termination triggers occur.

High level asks from our side:
- Narrow operator access to a bastion/jump box with ephemeral credentials; no persistent console admin for Redwood staff.
- A documented snapshot delivery process for forensic review (read-only snapshot + integrity proof).
- A KMS-handback or escrow-style key custody option for the model runtime keys in case of a provider insolvency or material breach.
- Defined audit cadence (30/60/90 day windows) and a reasonable on-site/remote witness plan.
- An Order Form exhibit listing the allowed scope of any operator actions (maintenance windows, emergency access, log review).

I attached a redline (BridgeMed_MSA_Redline_20280701.pdf) that our counsel prepared — it's conservative but shows what the procurement team needs to close. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the exhibit approach (Order Form + Exhibit for private deployments) and provide an internal security assessment and proposed edits?

We'd like to lock this in quickly; can you propose a short mutual action plan and an estimated review timeline? Our procurement ID is BM-PROC-9987.

Thanks,
Alex Burns
Head of Procurement, BridgeMed Health

1) For the snapshot delivery: do you need full filesystem-level forensic artifacts, or would an immutable L1 snapshot + signed hash + access to the runtime logs be sufficient?
2) For KMS handback: are you expecting a permanent handback of keys, or a time-limited escrow release trigger tied to the specific termination/insolvency events?
3) Is BridgeMed insisting on on-site witness (physical) or will remote witnessed validation be acceptable for the first round?

Alex / team — I reviewed the redline quickly and can confirm the asks are technically feasible with some guardrails. Summary of my security position:

- Operator Access: We can support an ephemeral bastion model with just-in-time sessions and session recording. We will require documented jump host IP blocks and a connectivity window. No persistent admin console credentials for Redwood engineers will be provisioned for standard production deployments.

- Snapshot / Forensic Delivery: We can provide a snapshot export (read-only) with a signed SHA256 hash and a notarized chain-of-custody manifest. For high-sensitivity customers we support an HSM-signed manifest. Deliverable options: remote transfer to an S3 bucket you control (preferred) or on-prem physical transfer for extreme cases.

- KMS/Escrow: We do not normally transfer long-term private keys. We can offer an escrow release mechanism where keys are transferred to a nominated TPA under explicit release conditions (insolvency, defined material breach). That will require a third-party escrow agreement and an exhibit describing triggers and verification steps.

- Audit windows: 30/60/90 windows are reasonable; we recommend a 48-hour advance request for remote witnessed assessments and a 14-day SLA for scheduling any on-site visit.

Suggested contract language bullets (I can formalize with Laura):
1) Define "Operator Access" with scope, allowed actions, IP allowlist, session capture, and emergency access process.
2) Define "Snapshot Transfer" deliverables, integrity proof, and acceptance criteria.
3) Define "Escrow/Key Release" triggers, TPA, and notarization requirements.
4) Add a security carveout limiting Redwood liabilities for third-party integrations required for customer-managed buckets.

I'll produce a short tech appendix and sample exhibit wording by Mon 7/4. Priyom — happy to review the BridgeMed redline and propose line edits.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Security, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form — private hosting operator access and audit exhibits

Alex — thanks for the redline and the clear checklist. We can accept the exhibit approach, but there are a few contract-level constraints we need to preserve for Redwood's exposure and for typical enterprise governance. High-level legal position follows.

Key contract items we will propose:
- Order Form Exhibit: we'll produce an Exhibit A (Private Deployment Exhibit) that enumerates allowed operator activities, maintenance windows, and the witness protocol. Exhibit will include an acceptance criteria table for snapshot handover.
- Escrow/Key Custody: we can agree to an escrow release to a named TPA under narrowly defined triggers. Redwood will require a clause limiting transfer of proprietary runtime artifacts and will seek an indemnity for misuse of keys after release.
- Audit/Inspection: agreed to scheduled remote audits and a limited number of remote witness validations per year. On-site audits will be permitted with reasonable notice; Redwood will charge for extraordinary on-site witness time beyond the standard allowance.
- Liability & SLA: any indemnity or access rights tied to operator actions must be coupled with reasonable liability caps and limitations for third-party software.

Timeline: legal redline + Exhibit A draft by Wed 7/7. We propose execution of the Order Form amendment on or before Fri 7/14, subject to BridgeMed's timely review.

I'll attach our internal mark-up and an Exhibit template in a follow-up; Priyom / Karthik, please confirm if you need any additional clauses included (e.g., data retention, log export frequency).

Laura Bennett
VP, Legal — Redwood Inference
